Do NOT load tools one at a time; each separate ToolSearch call wastes a full round-trip.**

Start a browser task whose tools are not yet loaded with a single call loading the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_close_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting. Only issue a second ToolSearch if the task later needs a tool you did not anticipate.

## claude.ai Claude Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>\n\n<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>\n\n<?claude block s1?>\n\n<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

While auto mode is active:

You can do much of your work through the Bash tool when it is the simpler route: read files with cat, head, or sed -n, search with grep and find, and make small, mechanical file changes with sed, heredocs, or short scripts instead of the dedicated Read, Edit, or Write tools. 1	---
2	title: "Generate Captions"
3	description: "Turn the speech in your clips into subtitles or word-by-word captions on a new track, on this Mac or with AssemblyAI."
4	---
5	
6	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
7	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
8	import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';
9	
10	Generate Captions transcribes the speech in your clips and lays it out on a new caption track as ordinary text clips, either as two-line subtitles or as large word-by-word captions.
11	
12	<AtAGlance
13	  menu="File ▸ Generate Captions…"
14	  tools="transcribe"
15	  needs={[
16	    'On this Mac: the language’s speech model, which the sheet can download.',
17	    'AssemblyAI: your own API key, unless every file is already transcribed.',
18	  ]}
19	/>
20	
21	## Generate captions
22	
23	<Steps>
24	
25	1. If you only want part of the project captioned, select those clips or mark an [in/out range](/timeline/in-out-range/).
26	
27	2. Choose **File ▸ Generate Captions…**. It has no keyboard shortcut. Playback pauses and the sheet opens.
28	
29	3. Set **Language**, **Engine**, **From** and **Style**, and look at the preview under the style.
30	
31	4. Check the summary line under the rows. It says how much audio the run covers.
32	
33	5. Choose **Generate**. The same card becomes a progress bar.
34	
35	</Steps>
36	
37	The captions go on a new track at the front, as one undo step. A run with nothing to report closes the sheet by itself.
38	
39	The menu item is greyed out when nothing on the open timeline can be transcribed. It needs at least one clip that plays sound from a media file, forwards, with its audio on. See [What can be transcribed](/captions/what-can-be-transcribed/).
40	
41	<Shot
42	  name="15-generate-captions-sheet.sheet"
43	  alt="The Generate Captions sheet, with Language set to English (United States), Engine to On this Mac, From to Whole timeline and Style to Subtitles. The three look boxes are greyed, a dark preview reads This is how it looks, Replace is greyed, and the summary reads 2 clips, 00:00:10.200 of audio."
44	/>
45	
46	## The sheet's rows
47	
48	From top to bottom:
49	
50	| Row | What it does | Default |
51	| --- | --- | --- |
52	| **Language:** | The [spoken language](#choose-a-language). | On this Mac: your Mac's own language, if it's on the list. AssemblyAI: Detect automatically. |
53	| **Engine:** | [Where the words are recognised](#choose-an-engine). | The engine you chose last time, On this Mac the first time |
54	| **Speakers:** | AssemblyAI only. "split by speaker, coloured in Subtitles". | Off |
55	| **Vocabulary:** | AssemblyAI only. Names and jargon to expect, separated by commas. | Empty |
56	| **Transcribe again:** | AssemblyAI only. "ignore any cached transcript". | Off |
57	| **From:** | [What to transcribe](#choose-what-to-transcribe). | Selected clips if the selection holds anything transcribable, else In/out range if a marked range does, else Whole timeline |
58	| **Style:** | [How the captions look](#choose-a-style). | The style you chose last time, Subtitles the first time |
59	| Three look boxes | **Slide the pill**, **Fill words as spoken** and **Dim in pauses**. See [Looks for word captions](/captions/word-caption-looks/). | Each as you last left it, off the first time |
60	| **Replace:** | [Swaps out earlier caption tracks](#replace-existing-captions) instead of adding another. | Off |
61	
62	[Transcribe with AssemblyAI](/captions/assemblyai-transcription/) explains the three AssemblyAI rows.
63	
64	## Choose what to transcribe
65	
66	**From:** offers **Selected clips**, **In/out range** and **Whole timeline**. A choice that holds nothing transcribable is greyed.
67	
68	**In/out range** takes every clip that overlaps the range, whole, so captions can run past the range's edges. Clips that can't be read don't count towards any of the three.
69	
70	## Choose an engine
71	
72	**Engine:** chooses where the words are recognised.
73	
74	| Engine | What happens |
75	| --- | --- |
76	| **On this Mac** | Recognition runs here and nothing is uploaded. The language's model has to be installed. See [Transcribe on this Mac](/captions/on-device-transcription/). |
77	| **AssemblyAI** | The audio of each file is uploaded and transcribed in the cloud, on your own key. See [Transcribe with AssemblyAI](/captions/assemblyai-transcription/). |
78	
79	The sentence at the top of the sheet changes with the engine to say what will happen to your audio. The **Speakers:**, **Vocabulary:** and **Transcribe again:** rows are hidden, not greyed, while the engine is **On this Mac**, and they appear when you choose **AssemblyAI**.
80	
81	## Choose a language
82	
83	The list depends on the engine, and changing the engine refills it.
84	
85	- **On this Mac:** every language this Mac's recogniser supports. One with no model reads "— not installed", and choosing it puts a **Download** row under **Language:**. [Transcribe on this Mac](/captions/on-device-transcription/) covers installing one.
86	- **AssemblyAI:** **Detect automatically**, then 21 rows: 18 languages, with English listed four ways.
87	
88	## Choose a style
89	
90	**Style:** picks subtitles or one of the five [word caption styles](/captions/word-caption-styles/).
91	
92	| Style | Typeface | Case |
93	| --- | --- | --- |
94	| **Subtitles** | Source Sans 3 | As written |
95	| **Highlight** | Montserrat Black | Upper case |
96	| **Pill** | Montserrat ExtraBold | Upper case |
97	| **Karaoke** | Montserrat ExtraBold | As written |
98	| **Build** | Anton | Upper case |
99	| **One Word** | Bebas Neue | Upper case |
100	
101	**Subtitles** cues use the **Caption** preset and hold at most two lines of 42 characters, for at most 6 seconds. See [Subtitles](/captions/subtitles/). Every other style fills each page by its measured width and carries each word's timing, so the word being said can be drawn differently.
102	
103	You choose a style when you generate. It isn't a preset you can apply in the inspector afterwards, so restyling means generating again. See [Restyle a caption track](/captions/restyle-captions/).
104	
105	## Check the sample preview
106	
107	Under the style and its look boxes is a sample page, drawn at this canvas's size, so you can see the style before you run anything. With **Subtitles**, it reads "This is how it looks" on a dark box when there are no cached words to use. [Word caption styles](/captions/word-caption-styles/) says how it behaves for a word style.
108	
109	## Replace existing captions
110	
111	By default, captions go on a new track, and earlier caption tracks stay where they are. Tick **Replace:** "existing captions" to swap out earlier caption tracks over the same clips instead. Removing them and placing the new captions happen in the same undo step.
112	
113	The box only works for a word style, with a track it may replace, and it's dimmed and unticked otherwise. While it's live, a line under it names what will go, such as "Replaces “Captions” (12 captions)." [Restyle a caption track](/captions/restyle-captions/) has the full rule.
114	
115	## Read the summary and the note
116	
117	Under the rows, a summary line gives the size of the run, for example `3 clips · 00:04:12.000 of audio`. With nothing to do, it reads "Nothing to transcribe". With AssemblyAI it prices the run instead. See [Transcribe with AssemblyAI](/captions/assemblyai-transcription/).
118	
119	Under that, a note explains anything stopping the run. With nothing transcribable, it reads "Only a clip whose media has sound can be transcribed, and never one played in reverse."
120	
121	**Generate** is greyed until the run can go ahead: while nothing can be transcribed, or while the chosen on-device language isn't installed. With AssemblyAI it also needs a key, unless every file is already transcribed.
122	
123	## Follow a run
124	
125	While a run goes, the card shows a progress bar, "Transcribing 3 clips…" and a detail line. With AssemblyAI it reads "Transcribing 3 clips with AssemblyAI…".
126	
127	On this Mac, the detail line names the clip being recognised. With AssemblyAI, it names the stage, and the bar is shared between files by their length.
128	
129	| Detail line | Where the file's share of the bar gets to |
130	| --- | --- |
131	| "Extracting interview.mov" | 25% |
132	| "Uploading interview.mov · 12 MB of 40" | 65% |
133	| "Submitting interview.mov" | Holds at 65% |
134	| "Waiting for AssemblyAI · 35 s" | 95% |
135	| "Saving interview.mov" | 100% |
136	
137	The wait advances on the clock, and it holds at 95% rather than pretending to finish.
138	
139	## Cancel a run
140	
141	Choose **Cancel** while a run goes. The detail line reads "Stopping…" until the run ends, then the card reads "The transcription was cancelled." and the button becomes **Close**. Nothing is placed. If the sheet closes mid-run, that stops the run too.
142	
143	Before a run starts, **Cancel** closes the sheet.
144	
145	## The run report
146	
147	Placing the captions is one undo step, **Generate Captions**.
148	
149	A clean run closes the sheet by itself. Otherwise the card stays open with **Close** and says what happened:
150	
151	- How many captions were added and on which track, for example "12 captions added on “Captions”."
152	- How many were shortened to fit.
153	- Which clips were skipped and why, for example "clip 7: no speech was recognised in it". The captions from the other clips are still placed.
154	- On a canvas taller than wide, how many Subtitles captions wrap to more than two lines.
155	
156	A cloud run can add more: a fallback model, the languages it detected, a delete AssemblyAI hasn't confirmed, or a transcript that couldn't be kept. See [Transcribe with AssemblyAI](/captions/assemblyai-transcription/) and [What goes to AssemblyAI](/captions/assemblyai-privacy/).
157	
158	A run that fails shows the error on the same card, and nothing is placed.
159	
160	| The card says | What it means |
161	| --- | --- |
162	| No speech was recognised in the audio that was transcribed. | Every clip was read, and none held any words. |
163	| The transcription failed: … | No captions came out, and at least one clip couldn't be read. It gives the first three reasons. |
164	| The project closed before the captions could be placed. | The project was gone by the time the run ended. |
165	
166	## What the sheet remembers
167	
168	Generate Captions reopens with your last **Engine:**, your last **Style:** and the three look boxes as you left them. Each is saved the moment you change it, whether or not you go on to generate.
169	
170	Everything else starts fresh each time, including **Language:**, **From:**, **Replace:** and the three AssemblyAI rows.
171	
172	## With an agent
173	
174	`transcribe` does what the sheet does, with these differences:
175	
176	- It can answer the captions without placing them, so an agent can read a transcript and check it first. That changes nothing in the project and makes no undo step.
177	- It never reads or writes what the sheet remembers. It uses the on-device engine and Subtitles unless it asks for something else, every time.
178	- It never downloads a language model. A language that isn't installed stops the call, and a person has to install it from the sheet.
179	
180	See [Tools: captions and transcripts](/mcp/tools-captions/).
181	
182	## Related
183	
184	- [What can be transcribed](/captions/what-can-be-transcribed/)
185	- [Transcribe on this Mac](/captions/on-device-transcription/)
186	- [Transcribe with AssemblyAI](/captions/assemblyai-transcription/)
187	- [Word caption styles](/captions/word-caption-styles/)
188	- [Looks for word captions](/captions/word-caption-looks/)
189	- [Captions are text clips](/captions/how-captions-work/)

1	---
2	title: "What can be transcribed"
3	description: "Which clips Generate Captions can read, why a clip gets left out of a run, and the limits on how much one run can do."
4	---
5	
6	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
7	
8	Before a run starts, Frame Job works out which clips it can read. This page says which those are, why a clip gets left out, and what limits a run.
9	
10	<AtAGlance menu="File ▸ Generate Captions…" tools="transcribe" />
11	
12	## Which clips can be transcribed
13	
14	A clip can be transcribed when all of these are true:
15	
16	- It plays a movie or sound file that has an audio track.
17	- It plays forwards.
18	- Its audio is on.
19	- Its file is present.
20	
21	**File ▸ Generate Captions…** is greyed out when no clip on the open timeline plays sound from a media file, forwards, with its audio on.
22	
23	## Why a clip is skipped
24	
25	A clip that can't be read isn't part of the run. In the [Generate Captions](/captions/generate-captions/) sheet it doesn't count towards the summary line, so if the sheet says 2 clips and you expected 3, the third is here. The sheet doesn't list these clips one by one. If it leaves nothing at all, it reads "Nothing to transcribe".
26	
27	An agent that names the clips it wants gets the reason back for each one, in these words:
28	
29	| Reason | What it means | What to do |
30	| --- | --- | --- |
31	| its source is not a media file, so it has no speech | It's a text, shape, still, image, graphic, adjustment or nest clip. | For a nest, [open it](/editing/inside-a-nest/) and caption inside it. |
32	| it plays in reverse, so its speech cannot be transcribed | The words would come out backwards. | Only a clip playing forwards can be read. See [Reverse a clip](/speed/reverse/). |
33	| its media has no audio track | The file has no sound. | Nothing to transcribe here. |
34	| its audio is switched off | For example, the picture half of a clip after [Detach Audio](/audio/detach-and-attach/). | After Detach Audio, the audio-only clip below it holds the sound and is read instead. **Clip ▸ Attach Audio** joins the two again. |
35	| its media file is missing | Frame Job can't find the file. | [Relink it](/projects/relink-media/). |
36	| its speed ramps, and no speed map was read for it | Frame Job couldn't work out where the ramp puts the words, so it won't guess. | |
37	| its speed or length is degenerate | The clip has no usable speed or no length. | |
38	
39	A clip that's read but holds no words shows up afterwards, in the [run report](/captions/generate-captions/#the-run-report), as "no speech was recognised in it".
40	
41	## Retimed clips land correctly
42	
43	On a sped-up, slowed or speed-ramped clip, each word lands where it's heard on the timeline, not where it sits in the file. Transcribing a ramped clip places each word where the ramp plays it.
44	
45	Captions keep following afterwards. Change the speed later and they move with the speech. See [Captions follow a speed change](/speed/captions-and-speed/).
46	
47	## The 10-hour and 4,096-clip limits
48	
49	**AssemblyAI takes at most 10 hours per file.** What counts is the length of the whole file, not the part your clip uses, because the whole file is what's sent. Frame Job won't extract or send a longer file, and its clips are listed in the [run report](/captions/generate-captions/#the-run-report) with "“name” is longer than AssemblyAI's 10-hour limit for one file." The other files in the run carry on.
50	
51	**On this Mac there's no limit on length.** There is a limit on time: each clip gets four times the length of its audio, and at least two minutes. A clip still going after that is stopped and reported with "Transcribing “name” took too long and was stopped."
52	
53	**A project holds at most 4,096 clips.** When a run's captions wouldn't fit, none of them are placed and the project doesn't change. The card says "5000 captions is more than this project has room for: 900 more clips would fit, out of 4096." Frame Job can only count captions once the words are in, so this comes at the end of the run. With **Replace** ticked, the clips on the tracks it would remove don't count against you.
54	
55	Every caption or page is one clip, so word styles usually use more clips than **Subtitles**, and **One Word** uses one clip for every word. [Limits](/reference/limits/) lists the rest of the project's limits.
56	
57	## Related
58	
59	- [Generate Captions](/captions/generate-captions/)
60	- [Transcribe on this Mac](/captions/on-device-transcription/)
61	- [Transcribe with AssemblyAI](/captions/assemblyai-transcription/)
62	- [Captions follow a speed change](/speed/captions-and-speed/)

---
title: "Captions are text clips"
description: "How captions behave in Frame Job: ordinary text clips on a track of their own, burned into the picture, with the same few rules however they were made."
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Every caption in Frame Job is an ordinary text clip on a track of its own. That one fact explains most of how captions behave: where they show up, how you change them, and what happens to them in an export.

<AtAGlance
  menu={['File ▸ Import Captions…', 'File ▸ Generate Captions…', 'File ▸ Export Captions…']}
  where="Inspector ▸ Clip tab ▸ Text"
  tools={['import_captions', 'transcribe', 'export_captions', 'render_frame', 'export']}
/>

## Get captions in and out

Three commands sit next to each other in the **File** menu. None of them has a keyboard shortcut.

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| [**File ▸ Import Captions…**](/captions/import-captions/) | Reads a SubRip (`.srt`) file onto a new caption track. |
| [**File ▸ Generate Captions…**](/captions/generate-captions/) | Transcribes the speech in your clips onto a new caption track. |
| [**File ▸ Export Captions…**](/captions/export-captions/) | Writes one track out as SubRip (`.srt`) or WebVTT (`.vtt`). |

## Captions are ordinary text clips

However a caption gets onto the timeline, it lands the same way: one text clip per caption, on a new track at the front of the stack, so it draws over everything else. An imported caption and a generated one are the same kind of thing afterwards.

So the tools you already use work on them:

- Drag a caption to retime it.
- Trim its edges, split it or delete it.
- Select a run of captions and restyle them together in the Clip tab, under **Text**.

[Edit captions](/captions/edit-captions/) covers what's particular to them, such as changing the words on a word caption.

## Captions burn in with no extra step

Captions are part of the picture, so the preview, an exported movie and a frame an agent renders all show them. There's nothing to switch on.

That also means an export always carries them burned in. They aren't a soft-subtitle track that a viewer can turn on and off. If you need that, write a separate subtitle file with [**File ▸ Export Captions…**](/captions/export-captions/).

## Two kinds of caption: subtitles and word captions

When you generate captions, the **Style** row chooses the kind.

| Kind | What you get |
| --- | --- |
| [Subtitles](/captions/subtitles/) | Classic two-line captions. |
| [Word captions](/captions/word-caption-styles/) | Large captions in one of five styles, where the word being said stands out. |

Speech is recognised [on this Mac](/captions/on-device-transcription/), with nothing uploaded, or [by AssemblyAI](/captions/assemblyai-transcription/) in the cloud, on your own key. Either engine can make either kind.

An imported file always comes in as plain text in the **Caption** preset, the look subtitles use.

## Caption track names

The first caption track is called **Captions**, then **Captions 2**, **Captions 3** and so on, taking the next free number, so you can tell separate runs apart in the track headers.

The name does some work. **Replace** in [Generate Captions](/captions/restyle-captions/), [**Re-lay Captions for This Canvas**](/captions/re-lay-captions/) and [captions following a speed change](/speed/captions-and-speed/) only touch a track called **Captions** or **Captions** and a number, and only when it holds nothing but text clips. [Rename a track](/timeline/manage-tracks/) to anything else and all three leave it alone.

## A caption track is never guessed

Nothing in a project marks a track as the caption track. A name alone doesn't make one, and you can rename a track whenever you like. So a command that writes a caption file shows you the choice instead of assuming.

Any track can be exported when it has at least one clip, every clip on it is a text clip, and at least one of those clips has text. A track of titles qualifies as well.

[**File ▸ Export Captions…**](/captions/export-captions/) lists every such track in its **Track** pop-up, front-most first, with the front-most selected. With only one to choose from, the pop-up is greyed. With none, the menu item is greyed.

An agent has no pop-up to look at. When a project has several such tracks and the agent doesn't name one, `export_captions` won't pick for it, and it answers with the list. With none, it says there are no captions to write.

## Frame grid and no overlaps

These rules apply to every caption that's imported or generated.

- **Times land on frames.** Every caption's start and end snap to the nearest frame of the project, so a caption can come out up to a frame shorter or longer than its source says. A caption that would snap to no length at all gets one frame.
- **Captions on one track never overlap.** When a caption starts before the previous one ends, the earlier one is cut back to meet it, and the run reports how many were shortened.
- **A caption needs at least one frame.** One that would be left shorter than that is skipped and reported.

## Captions inside a nest

The caption commands work on the timeline you have open. With a [nest open](/editing/inside-a-nest/):

- **Import Captions…** and **Generate Captions…** put the new track at the front of the nest.
- **Export Captions…** lists that nest's tracks.

To caption the main timeline, close the nest first.

## Related

- [Import captions](/captions/import-captions/)
- [Generate Captions](/captions/generate-captions/)
- [Edit captions](/captions/edit-captions/)
- [Export captions](/captions/export-captions/)
- [Text clips](/text-and-shapes/text-clips/)
---
title: "Import captions"
description: "Bring a SubRip (.srt) caption file onto the timeline as text clips, and see what Frame Job copes with, removes and reports along the way."
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Import Captions reads a SubRip (`.srt`) file onto a new caption track, one text clip per caption, as a single undo step. Use it when someone has already written the captions.

<AtAGlance menu="File ▸ Import Captions…" tools="import_captions" />

## Import captions

<Steps>

1. Choose **File ▸ Import Captions…**. It has no keyboard shortcut, and it's available whenever the project window has no sheet open.

2. Pick the file. The open panel reads "Choose a SubRip (.srt) caption file." It accepts `.srt` and any plain-text file, so a SubRip file saved as `.txt` imports too.

</Steps>

Each caption becomes one text clip in the [**Caption** preset](/text-and-shapes/text-presets/), on a new track at the front called **Captions**, or the next free number. Undo removes the lot in one step, **Import Captions**. With a [nest](/editing/inside-a-nest/) open, the track goes at the front of the nest.

A clean import shows no message. If there's anything to tell you, an alert appears when it finishes. See [Malformed entries are reported](#malformed-entries-are-reported).

A caption file comes in through this command, not as media.

## What the reader tolerates

Real SubRip files vary, and Frame Job copes with these variations rather than turning the file away:

- A UTF-8 byte-order mark.
- Windows (CRLF) or old Mac (bare CR) line endings.
- A missing index line above the timing line.
- A comma or a dot before the milliseconds.
- The `MM:SS` and `SS` shorthands, and up to nine digits after the seconds.
- Position settings after the end time, which are ignored.
- Text in UTF-8, or in UTF-16 with a byte-order mark.

## What happens to the text

A text clip holds one plain string, so formatting that can't be kept is removed rather than shown as angle brackets on the canvas.

| In the file | What happens |
| --- | --- |
| `<i>`, `<b>`, `<u>`, `<font …>` and their closing tags | Removed, along with anything else shaped like a tag: a `<` followed by a letter, or by `/` and a letter, up to the next `>`. |
| `{\an8}`-style overrides | Removed: a `{\` up to the next `}`. |
| `&` `<` `>` `"` `'` `'` ` ` | Decoded to the character they stand for. |
| Text that only looks like a tag, such as `<<` or `a < b` | Stays as text. |

The file's own line breaks are kept, and long lines also wrap inside the caption box, which is 80% of the canvas width.

## What happens to the timing

Every time snaps to the project's frame grid. A caption that starts before the previous one ends cuts the earlier one back to meet it. A caption left shorter than one frame is skipped. [Frame grid and no overlaps](/captions/how-captions-work/#frame-grid-and-no-overlaps) has the rules.

## Malformed entries are reported

Frame Job skips an entry it can't read, carries on with the rest, and tells you. Nothing is dropped silently.

When the import finishes with something to report, an alert headed "Imported 42 captions from “interview.srt”." says how many captions were shortened to fit and lists what was skipped by line number. It shows the first eight, then "…and N more."

| The alert says | What's wrong with the entry |
| --- | --- |
| no “-->” timing line in this entry | The block has no timing line. |
| “…” is not a HH:MM:SS,mmm time | A time can't be read. A time past 1,000,000 seconds, about 277 hours, counts as unreadable. |
| two “-->” in one timing line | The timing line has more than one arrow. |
| 2 lines before the timing line | More than an index line sits above the timing line. |
| ends at or before it starts | The end time isn't after the start time. |
| no caption text | The entry has timing but no words, or nothing left once markup is removed. |
| starts less than a frame before the next caption | Shortening it to fit would leave it under one frame. |

On a canvas taller than wide, the alert also says when captions wrap to more than two lines. See [Subtitles](/captions/subtitles/).

## When a file can't be read

If not one caption in a file can be read, Frame Job imports nothing and the project doesn't change.

| The message says | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| No captions could be read from “name.srt”. | Every entry failed. The message gives the first three reasons. |
| “name.srt” could not be read as text. | The file couldn't be opened. |
| “name.srt” holds 5000 captions, more than this project has room for: 900 more clips would fit, out of 4096. | The file would take the project past its 4,096-clip limit. |

## Good to know

Save a caption file as UTF-8 before you import it. A file in an older encoding such as Windows-1252 or Latin-1 is fine with no accented letters in it, but with them the import usually stops with “No captions could be read”. If one does import, its accented letters may come out wrong.

## With an agent

`import_captions` can put the captions on a track that already exists, which the menu can't. Captions that would overlap something on that track are dropped, so leaving it to make a new track is the safer choice. It reports what landed and each malformed entry by line. See [Tools: captions and transcripts](/mcp/tools-captions/).

## Related

- [Captions are text clips](/captions/how-captions-work/)
- [Edit captions](/captions/edit-captions/)
- [Export captions](/captions/export-captions/)
- [Generate Captions](/captions/generate-captions/)

1	---
2	title: "Generate Captions"
3	description: "Turn the speech in your clips into subtitles or word-by-word captions on a new track, on this Mac or with AssemblyAI."
4	---
5	
6	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
7	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
8	import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';
9	
10	Generate Captions transcribes the speech in your clips and lays it out on a new caption track as ordinary text clips, either as two-line subtitles or as large word-by-word captions.
11	
12	<AtAGlance
13	  menu="File ▸ Generate Captions…"
14	  tools="transcribe"
15	  needs={[
16	    'On this Mac: the language’s speech model, which the sheet can download.',
17	    'AssemblyAI: your own API key, unless every file is already transcribed.',
18	  ]}
19	/>
20	
21	## Generate captions
22	
23	<Steps>
24	
25	1. If you only want part of the project captioned, select those clips or mark an [in/out range](/timeline/in-out-range/).
26	
27	2. Choose **File ▸ Generate Captions…**. It has no keyboard shortcut. Playback pauses and the sheet opens.
28	
29	3. Set **Language**, **Engine**, **From** and **Style**, and look at the preview under the style.
30	
31	4. Check the summary line under the rows. It says how much audio the run covers.
32	
33	5. Choose **Generate**. The same card becomes a progress bar.
34	
35	</Steps>
36	
37	The captions go on a new track at the front, as one undo step. A run with nothing to report closes the sheet by itself.
38	
39	The menu item is greyed out when nothing on the open timeline can be transcribed. It needs at least one clip that plays sound from a media file, forwards, with its audio on. See [What can be transcribed](/captions/what-can-be-transcribed/).
40	
41	<Shot
42	  name="15-generate-captions-sheet.sheet"
43	  alt="The Generate Captions sheet, with Language set to English (United States), Engine to On this Mac, From to Whole timeline and Style to Subtitles. The three look boxes are greyed, a dark preview reads This is how it looks, Replace is greyed, and the summary reads 2 clips, 00:00:10.200 of audio."
44	/>
45	
46	## The sheet's rows
47	
48	From top to bottom:
49	
50	| Row | What it does | Default |
51	| --- | --- | --- |
52	| **Language:** | The [spoken language](#choose-a-language). | On this Mac: your Mac's own language, if it's on the list. AssemblyAI: Detect automatically. |
53	| **Engine:** | [Where the words are recognised](#choose-an-engine). | The engine you chose last time, On this Mac the first time |
54	| **Speakers:** | AssemblyAI only. "split by speaker, coloured in Subtitles". | Off |
55	| **Vocabulary:** | AssemblyAI only. Names and jargon to expect, separated by commas. | Empty |
56	| **Transcribe again:** | AssemblyAI only. "ignore any cached transcript". | Off |
57	| **From:** | [What to transcribe](#choose-what-to-transcribe). | Selected clips if the selection holds anything transcribable, else In/out range if a marked range does, else Whole timeline |
58	| **Style:** | [How the captions look](#choose-a-style). | The style you chose last time, Subtitles the first time |
59	| Three look boxes | **Slide the pill**, **Fill words as spoken** and **Dim in pauses**. See [Looks for word captions](/captions/word-caption-looks/). | Each as you last left it, off the first time |
60	| **Replace:** | [Swaps out earlier caption tracks](#replace-existing-captions) instead of adding another. | Off |
61	
62	[Transcribe with AssemblyAI](/captions/assemblyai-transcription/) explains the three AssemblyAI rows.
63	
64	## Choose what to transcribe
65	
66	**From:** offers **Selected clips**, **In/out range** and **Whole timeline**. A choice that holds nothing transcribable is greyed.
67	
68	**In/out range** takes every clip that overlaps the range, whole, so captions can run past the range's edges. Clips that can't be read don't count towards any of the three.
69	
70	## Choose an engine
71	
72	**Engine:** chooses where the words are recognised.
73	
74	| Engine | What happens |
75	| --- | --- |
76	| **On this Mac** | Recognition runs here and nothing is uploaded. The language's model has to be installed. See [Transcribe on this Mac](/captions/on-device-transcription/). |
77	| **AssemblyAI** | The audio of each file is uploaded and transcribed in the cloud, on your own key. See [Transcribe with AssemblyAI](/captions/assemblyai-transcription/). |
78	
79	The sentence at the top of the sheet changes with the engine to say what will happen to your audio. The **Speakers:**, **Vocabulary:** and **Transcribe again:** rows are hidden, not greyed, while the engine is **On this Mac**, and they appear when you choose **AssemblyAI**.
80	
81	## Choose a language
82	
83	The list depends on the engine, and changing the engine refills it.
84	
85	- **On this Mac:** every language this Mac's recogniser supports. One with no model reads "— not installed", and choosing it puts a **Download** row under **Language:**. [Transcribe on this Mac](/captions/on-device-transcription/) covers installing one.
86	- **AssemblyAI:** **Detect automatically**, then 21 rows: 18 languages, with English listed four ways.
87	
88	## Choose a style
89	
90	**Style:** picks subtitles or one of the five [word caption styles](/captions/word-caption-styles/).
91	
92	| Style | Typeface | Case |
93	| --- | --- | --- |
94	| **Subtitles** | Source Sans 3 | As written |
95	| **Highlight** | Montserrat Black | Upper case |
96	| **Pill** | Montserrat ExtraBold | Upper case |
97	| **Karaoke** | Montserrat ExtraBold | As written |
98	| **Build** | Anton | Upper case |
99	| **One Word** | Bebas Neue | Upper case |
100	
101	**Subtitles** cues use the **Caption** preset and hold at most two lines of 42 characters, for at most 6 seconds. See [Subtitles](/captions/subtitles/). Every other style fills each page by its measured width and carries each word's timing, so the word being said can be drawn differently.
102	
103	You choose a style when you generate. It isn't a preset you can apply in the inspector afterwards, so restyling means generating again. See [Restyle a caption track](/captions/restyle-captions/).
104	
105	## Check the sample preview
106	
107	Under the style and its look boxes is a sample page, drawn at this canvas's size, so you can see the style before you run anything. With **Subtitles**, it reads "This is how it looks" on a dark box when there are no cached words to use. [Word caption styles](/captions/word-caption-styles/) says how it behaves for a word style.
108	
109	## Replace existing captions
110	
111	By default, captions go on a new track, and earlier caption tracks stay where they are. Tick **Replace:** "existing captions" to swap out earlier caption tracks over the same clips instead. Removing them and placing the new captions happen in the same undo step.
112	
113	The box only works for a word style, with a track it may replace, and it's dimmed and unticked otherwise. While it's live, a line under it names what will go, such as "Replaces “Captions” (12 captions)." [Restyle a caption track](/captions/restyle-captions/) has the full rule.
114	
115	## Read the summary and the note
116	
117	Under the rows, a summary line gives the size of the run, for example `3 clips · 00:04:12.000 of audio`. With nothing to do, it reads "Nothing to transcribe". With AssemblyAI it prices the run instead. See [Transcribe with AssemblyAI](/captions/assemblyai-transcription/).
118	
119	Under that, a note explains anything stopping the run. With nothing transcribable, it reads "Only a clip whose media has sound can be transcribed, and never one played in reverse."
120	
121	**Generate** is greyed until the run can go ahead: while nothing can be transcribed, or while the chosen on-device language isn't installed. With AssemblyAI it also needs a key, unless every file is already transcribed.
122	
123	## Follow a run
124	
125	While a run goes, the card shows a progress bar, "Transcribing 3 clips…" and a detail line. With AssemblyAI it reads "Transcribing 3 clips with AssemblyAI…".
126	
127	On this Mac, the detail line names the clip being recognised. With AssemblyAI, it names the stage, and the bar is shared between files by their length.
128	
129	| Detail line | Where the file's share of the bar gets to |
130	| --- | --- |
131	| "Extracting interview.mov" | 25% |
132	| "Uploading interview.mov · 12 MB of 40" | 65% |
133	| "Submitting interview.mov" | Holds at 65% |
134	| "Waiting for AssemblyAI · 35 s" | 95% |
135	| "Saving interview.mov" | 100% |
136	
137	The wait advances on the clock, and it holds at 95% rather than pretending to finish.
138	
139	## Cancel a run
140	
141	Choose **Cancel** while a run goes. The detail line reads "Stopping…" until the run ends, then the card reads "The transcription was cancelled." and the button becomes **Close**. Nothing is placed. If the sheet closes mid-run, that stops the run too.
142	
143	Before a run starts, **Cancel** closes the sheet.
144	
145	## The run report
146	
147	Placing the captions is one undo step, **Generate Captions**.
148	
149	A clean run closes the sheet by itself. Otherwise the card stays open with **Close** and says what happened:
150	
151	- How many captions were added and on which track, for example "12 captions added on “Captions”."
152	- How many were shortened to fit.
153	- Which clips were skipped and why, for example "clip 7: no speech was recognised in it". The captions from the other clips are still placed.
154	- On a canvas taller than wide, how many Subtitles captions wrap to more than two lines.
155	
156	A cloud run can add more: a fallback model, the languages it detected, a delete AssemblyAI hasn't confirmed, or a transcript that couldn't be kept. See [Transcribe with AssemblyAI](/captions/assemblyai-transcription/) and [What goes to AssemblyAI](/captions/assemblyai-privacy/).
157	
158	A run that fails shows the error on the same card, and nothing is placed.
159	
160	| The card says | What it means |
161	| --- | --- |
162	| No speech was recognised in the audio that was transcribed. | Every clip was read, and none held any words. |
163	| The transcription failed: … | No captions came out, and at least one clip couldn't be read. It gives the first three reasons. |
164	| The project closed before the captions could be placed. | The project was gone by the time the run ended. |
165	
166	## What the sheet remembers
167	
168	Generate Captions reopens with your last **Engine:**, your last **Style:** and the three look boxes as you left them. Each is saved the moment you change it, whether or not you go on to generate.
169	
170	Everything else starts fresh each time, including **Language:**, **From:**, **Replace:** and the three AssemblyAI rows.
171	
172	## With an agent
173	
174	`transcribe` does what the sheet does, with these differences:
175	
176	- It can answer the captions without placing them, so an agent can read a transcript and check it first. That changes nothing in the project and makes no undo step.
177	- It never reads or writes what the sheet remembers. It uses the on-device engine and Subtitles unless it asks for something else, every time.
178	- It never downloads a language model. A language that isn't installed stops the call, and a person has to install it from the sheet.
179	
180	See [Tools: captions and transcripts](/mcp/tools-captions/).
181	
182	## Related
183	
184	- [What can be transcribed](/captions/what-can-be-transcribed/)
185	- [Transcribe on this Mac](/captions/on-device-transcription/)
186	- [Transcribe with AssemblyAI](/captions/assemblyai-transcription/)
187	- [Word caption styles](/captions/word-caption-styles/)
188	- [Looks for word captions](/captions/word-caption-looks/)
189	- [Captions are text clips](/captions/how-captions-work/)

2	title: "What can be transcribed"
3	description: "Which clips Generate Captions can read, why a clip gets left out of a run, and the limits on how much one run can do."
4	---
5	
6	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
7	
8	Before a run starts, Frame Job works out which clips it can read. This page says which those are, why a clip gets left out, and what limits a run.
9	
10	<AtAGlance menu="File ▸ Generate Captions…" tools="transcribe" />
11	
12	## Which clips can be transcribed
13	
14	A clip can be transcribed when all of these are true:
15	
16	- It plays a movie or sound file that has an audio track.
17	- It plays forwards.
18	- Its audio is on.
19	- Its file is present.
20	
21	**File ▸ Generate Captions…** is greyed out when no clip on the open timeline plays sound from a media file, forwards, with its audio on.
22	
23	## Why a clip is skipped
24	
25	A clip that can't be read isn't part of the run. In the [Generate Captions](/captions/generate-captions/) sheet it doesn't count towards the summary line, so if the sheet says 2 clips and you expected 3, the third is here. The sheet doesn't list these clips one by one. If it leaves nothing at all, it reads "Nothing to transcribe".
26	
27	An agent that names the clips it wants gets the reason back for each one, in these words:
28	
29	| Reason | What it means | What to do |
30	| --- | --- | --- |
31	| its source is not a media file, so it has no speech | It's a text, shape, still, image, graphic, adjustment or nest clip. | For a nest, [open it](/editing/inside-a-nest/) and caption inside it. |
32	| it plays in reverse, so its speech cannot be transcribed | The words would come out backwards. | Only a clip playing forwards can be read. See [Reverse a clip](/speed/reverse/). |
33	| its media has no audio track | The file has no sound. | Nothing to transcribe here. |
34	| its audio is switched off | For example, the picture half of a clip after [Detach Audio](/audio/detach-and-attach/). | After Detach Audio, the audio-only clip below it holds the sound and is read instead. **Clip ▸ Attach Audio** joins the two again. |
35	| its media file is missing | Frame Job can't find the file. | [Relink it](/projects/relink-media/). |
36	| its speed ramps, and no speed map was read for it | Frame Job couldn't work out where the ramp puts the words, so it won't guess. | |
37	| its speed or length is degenerate | The clip has no usable speed or no length. | |
38	
39	A clip that's read but holds no words shows up afterwards, in the [run report](/captions/generate-captions/#the-run-report), as "no speech was recognised in it".
40	
41	## Retimed clips land correctly
42	
43	On a sped-up, slowed or speed-ramped clip, each word lands where it's heard on the timeline, not where it sits in the file. Transcribing a ramped clip places each word where the ramp plays it.
44	
45	Captions keep following afterwards. Change the speed later and they move with the speech. See [Captions follow a speed change](/speed/captions-and-speed/).
46	
47	## The 10-hour and 4,096-clip limits
48	
49	**AssemblyAI takes at most 10 hours per file.** What counts is the length of the whole file, not the part your clip uses, because the whole file is what's sent. Frame Job won't extract or send a longer file, and its clips are listed in the [run report](/captions/generate-captions/#the-run-report) with "“name” is longer than AssemblyAI's 10-hour limit for one file." The other files in the run carry on.
50	
51	**On this Mac there's no limit on length.** There is a limit on time: each clip gets four times the length of its audio, and at least two minutes. A clip still going after that is stopped and reported with "Transcribing “name” took too long and was stopped."
52	
53	**A project holds at most 4,096 clips.** When a run's captions wouldn't fit, none of them are placed and the project doesn't change. The card says "5000 captions is more than this project has room for: 900 more clips would fit, out of 4096." Frame Job can only count captions once the words are in, so this comes at the end of the run. With **Replace** ticked, the clips on the tracks it would remove don't count against you.
54	
55	Every caption or page is one clip, so word styles usually use more clips than **Subtitles**, and **One Word** uses one clip for every word. [Limits](/reference/limits/) lists the rest of the project's limits.
56	
57	## Related

61	- [Transcribe with AssemblyAI](/captions/assemblyai-transcription/)

---
title: "Captions are text clips"
description: "How captions behave in Frame Job: ordinary text clips on a track of their own, burned into the picture, with the same few rules however they were made."
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Every caption in Frame Job is an ordinary text clip on a track of its own. That one fact explains most of how captions behave: where they show up, how you change them, and what happens to them in an export.

<AtAGlance
  menu={['File ▸ Import Captions…', 'File ▸ Generate Captions…', 'File ▸ Export Captions…']}
  where="Inspector ▸ Clip tab ▸ Text"
  tools={['import_captions', 'transcribe', 'export_captions', 'render_frame', 'export']}
/>

## Get captions in and out

Three commands sit next to each other in the **File** menu. None of them has a keyboard shortcut.

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| [**File ▸ Import Captions…**](/captions/import-captions/) | Reads a SubRip (`.srt`) file onto a new caption track. |
| [**File ▸ Generate Captions…**](/captions/generate-captions/) | Transcribes the speech in your clips onto a new caption track. |
| [**File ▸ Export Captions…**](/captions/export-captions/) | Writes one track out as SubRip (`.srt`) or WebVTT (`.vtt`). |

## Captions are ordinary text clips

However a caption gets onto the timeline, it lands the same way: one text clip per caption, on a new track at the front of the stack, so it draws over everything else. An imported caption and a generated one are the same kind of thing afterwards.

So the tools you already use work on them:

- Drag a caption to retime it.
- Trim its edges, split it or delete it.
- Select a run of captions and restyle them together in the Clip tab, under **Text**.

[Edit captions](/captions/edit-captions/) covers what's particular to them, such as changing the words on a word caption.

## Captions burn in with no extra step

Captions are part of the picture, so the preview, an exported movie and a frame an agent renders all show them. There's nothing to switch on.

That also means an export always carries them burned in. They aren't a soft-subtitle track that a viewer can turn on and off. If you need that, write a separate subtitle file with [**File ▸ Export Captions…**](/captions/export-captions/).

## Two kinds of caption: subtitles and word captions

When you generate captions, the **Style** row chooses the kind.

| Kind | What you get |
| --- | --- |
| [Subtitles](/captions/subtitles/) | Classic two-line captions. |
| [Word captions](/captions/word-caption-styles/) | Large captions in one of five styles, where the word being said stands out. |

Speech is recognised [on this Mac](/captions/on-device-transcription/), with nothing uploaded, or [by AssemblyAI](/captions/assemblyai-transcription/) in the cloud, on your own key. Either engine can make either kind.

An imported file always comes in as plain text in the **Caption** preset, the look subtitles use.

## Caption track names

The first caption track is called **Captions**, then **Captions 2**, **Captions 3** and so on, taking the next free number, so you can tell separate runs apart in the track headers.

The name does some work. **Replace** in [Generate Captions](/captions/restyle-captions/), [**Re-lay Captions for This Canvas**](/captions/re-lay-captions/) and [captions following a speed change](/speed/captions-and-speed/) only touch a track called **Captions** or **Captions** and a number, and only when it holds nothing but text clips. [Rename a track](/timeline/manage-tracks/) to anything else and all three leave it alone.

## A caption track is never guessed

Nothing in a project marks a track as the caption track. A name alone doesn't make one, and you can rename a track whenever you like. So a command that writes a caption file shows you the choice instead of assuming.

Any track can be exported when it has at least one clip, every clip on it is a text clip, and at least one of those clips has text. A track of titles qualifies as well.

[**File ▸ Export Captions…**](/captions/export-captions/) lists every such track in its **Track** pop-up, front-most first, with the front-most selected. With only one to choose from, the pop-up is greyed. With none, the menu item is greyed.

An agent has no pop-up to look at. When a project has several such tracks and the agent doesn't name one, `export_captions` won't pick for it, and it answers with the list. With none, it says there are no captions to write.

## Frame grid and no overlaps

These rules apply to every caption that's imported or generated.

- **Times land on frames.** Every caption's start and end snap to the nearest frame of the project, so a caption can come out up to a frame shorter or longer than its source says. A caption that would snap to no length at all gets one frame.
- **Captions on one track never overlap.** When a caption starts before the previous one ends, the earlier one is cut back to meet it, and the run reports how many were shortened.
- **A caption needs at least one frame.** One that would be left shorter than that is skipped and reported.

## Captions inside a nest

The caption commands work on the timeline you have open. With a [nest open](/editing/inside-a-nest/):

- **Import Captions…** and **Generate Captions…** put the new track at the front of the nest.
- **Export Captions…** lists that nest's tracks.

To caption the main timeline, close the nest first.

## Related

- [Import captions](/captions/import-captions/)
- [Generate Captions](/captions/generate-captions/)
- [Edit captions](/captions/edit-captions/)
- [Export captions](/captions/export-captions/)
- [Text clips](/text-and-shapes/text-clips/)
---
title: "Import captions"
description: "Bring a SubRip (.srt) caption file onto the timeline as text clips, and see what Frame Job copes with, removes and reports along the way."
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Import Captions reads a SubRip (`.srt`) file onto a new caption track, one text clip per caption, as a single undo step. Use it when someone has already written the captions.

<AtAGlance menu="File ▸ Import Captions…" tools="import_captions" />

## Import captions

<Steps>

1. Choose **File ▸ Import Captions…**. It has no keyboard shortcut, and it's available whenever the project window has no sheet open.

2. Pick the file. The open panel reads "Choose a SubRip (.srt) caption file." It accepts `.srt` and any plain-text file, so a SubRip file saved as `.txt` imports too.

</Steps>

Each caption becomes one text clip in the [**Caption** preset](/text-and-shapes/text-presets/), on a new track at the front called **Captions**, or the next free number. Undo removes the lot in one step, **Import Captions**. With a [nest](/editing/inside-a-nest/) open, the track goes at the front of the nest.

A clean import shows no message. If there's anything to tell you, an alert appears when it finishes. See [Malformed entries are reported](#malformed-entries-are-reported).

A caption file comes in through this command, not as media.

## What the reader tolerates

Real SubRip files vary, and Frame Job copes with these variations rather than turning the file away:

- A UTF-8 byte-order mark.
- Windows (CRLF) or old Mac (bare CR) line endings.
- A missing index line above the timing line.
- A comma or a dot before the milliseconds.
- The `MM:SS` and `SS` shorthands, and up to nine digits after the seconds.
- Position settings after the end time, which are ignored.
- Text in UTF-8, or in UTF-16 with a byte-order mark.

## What happens to the text

A text clip holds one plain string, so formatting that can't be kept is removed rather than shown as angle brackets on the canvas.

| In the file | What happens |
| --- | --- |
| `<i>`, `<b>`, `<u>`, `<font …>` and their closing tags | Removed, along with anything else shaped like a tag: a `<` followed by a letter, or by `/` and a letter, up to the next `>`. |
| `{\an8}`-style overrides | Removed: a `{\` up to the next `}`. |
| `&` `<` `>` `"` `'` `'` ` ` | Decoded to the character they stand for. |
| Text that only looks like a tag, such as `<<` or `a < b` | Stays as text. |

The file's own line breaks are kept, and long lines also wrap inside the caption box, which is 80% of the canvas width.

## What happens to the timing

Every time snaps to the project's frame grid. A caption that starts before the previous one ends cuts the earlier one back to meet it. A caption left shorter than one frame is skipped. [Frame grid and no overlaps](/captions/how-captions-work/#frame-grid-and-no-overlaps) has the rules.

## Malformed entries are reported

Frame Job skips an entry it can't read, carries on with the rest, and tells you. Nothing is dropped silently.

When the import finishes with something to report, an alert headed "Imported 42 captions from “interview.srt”." says how many captions were shortened to fit and lists what was skipped by line number. It shows the first eight, then "…and N more."

| The alert says | What's wrong with the entry |
| --- | --- |
| no “-->” timing line in this entry | The block has no timing line. |
| “…” is not a HH:MM:SS,mmm time | A time can't be read. A time past 1,000,000 seconds, about 277 hours, counts as unreadable. |
| two “-->” in one timing line | The timing line has more than one arrow. |
| 2 lines before the timing line | More than an index line sits above the timing line. |
| ends at or before it starts | The end time isn't after the start time. |
| no caption text | The entry has timing but no words, or nothing left once markup is removed. |
| starts less than a frame before the next caption | Shortening it to fit would leave it under one frame. |

On a canvas taller than wide, the alert also says when captions wrap to more than two lines. See [Subtitles](/captions/subtitles/).

## When a file can't be read

If not one caption in a file can be read, Frame Job imports nothing and the project doesn't change.

| The message says | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| No captions could be read from “name.srt”. | Every entry failed. The message gives the first three reasons. |
| “name.srt” could not be read as text. | The file couldn't be opened. |
| “name.srt” holds 5000 captions, more than this project has room for: 900 more clips would fit, out of 4096. | The file would take the project past its 4,096-clip limit. |

## Good to know

Save a caption file as UTF-8 before you import it. A file in an older encoding such as Windows-1252 or Latin-1 is fine with no accented letters in it, but with them the import usually stops with “No captions could be read”. If one does import, its accented letters may come out wrong.

## With an agent

`import_captions` can put the captions on a track that already exists, which the menu can't. Captions that would overlap something on that track are dropped, so leaving it to make a new track is the safer choice. It reports what landed and each malformed entry by line. See [Tools: captions and transcripts](/mcp/tools-captions/).

- [Edit captions](/captions/edit-captions/)
- [Export captions](/captions/export-captions/)
- [Generate Captions](/captions/generate-captions/)

/// own `isEnabled` — never inside it.
///
/// **Closing the sheet mid-download is a decision, not code**: the download
/// runs on in the framework, and the observation dies with this controller
/// (`[weak self]`).
extension TranscribeSheetController {

    /// Grid row 1: an empty label cell, and the button, the bar and the
    /// label in one stack.
    func makeDownloadRow() -> [NSView] {
        let button = NSButton(
            title: "Download", target: self, action: #selector(downloadClicked(_:)))

98:Once a run starts, a clip that fails is listed under `skipped` and the others are still placed. That includes a clip whose file is over AssemblyAI's 10-hour limit, and a clip where no speech was heard. The exception is a key AssemblyAI refuses, which ends the run with nothing placed, because every later file would fail the same way. If no cues come out of the whole run, nothing is placed and the answer says why, for example "No speech was recognised in the audio that was transcribed."
102:### Transcribe engines
104:**`apple`** is the default. Speech recognition runs on this Mac and nothing leaves it. It needs no permission and has no length limit. Each run recognises the audio again, because this engine keeps nothing for `transcribe` to reuse, and `refresh` doesn't apply.
125:Both need `engine: "assemblyai"`. The sheet's rows are described on [Transcribe with AssemblyAI](/captions/assemblyai-transcription/#split-the-words-by-speaker).
177:To change a word style, run `transcribe` again with `replace: true`. See [Restyle a caption track](/captions/restyle-captions/).
179:`replace` removes, in the same undo step, every track this command could have made over these clips: a track named **Captions** or **Captions N** that holds only text clips, each of which overlaps a clip being transcribed. The answer lists those tracks under `replaced`.
183:## `import_captions`
241:**Round trips.** Exported and brought back with `import_captions`, every cue returns to the tick it was written from, at every ordinary frame rate. The file itself may not match one you first imported. See [Frame-exact round trips](/captions/export-captions/#frame-exact-round-trips).
309:The words come from the file's current AssemblyAI transcript, kept in the project, when it has one. That transcript comes from an earlier AssemblyAI run, such as [`transcribe`](#transcribe) or the sheet. Otherwise this Mac's own speech recogniser runs over the clip, which takes seconds per minute of speech. Reading never uses the network and needs no key.
311:- **Where a word starts.** An on-device word's start is moved to where its sound begins, using the file's voice detection and waveform. The recogniser's own start is often early, inside the pause before the word. Until voice detection has finished with the file, starts are the recogniser's and `note` says so, so ask again once it has. AssemblyAI words and every word's end are as transcribed.
